Gibraltar.title: Guide: Tax Return in Gibraltar
Gibraltar.intro: Gibraltar offers two main taxation systems for residents: ABS (Allowance Based System) and GIBS (Gross Income Based System). This guide will help you understand both systems and complete your declaration.

dates.title: Important Dates
dates.payments: Important: Payments on account are usually made in January and July

abs.title: ABS System (Allowance Based System)
abs.whatIsDesc: Traditional system based on allowances (personal deductions) and progressive tax rates.
allowances: Married Allowance: Additional £3,000 if you are married
Mortgage Interest Relief: Deduction of mortgage interests (limited to £25,000)

gibs.title: GIBS System (Gross Income Based System)
gibs.whatIsDesc: Simplified system introduced in 2010. Applies a fixed rate on gross income, without significant deductions. Simpler but may result in higher taxation for some people.
features: Minor Adjustments: Small reductions for family circumstances

comparison.title: ABS or GIBS? Which one to choose?
absBest: You are married or have children
You have a mortgage with high interest
gibsBest: You are single with no children
You have no mortgage or deductions

specialCases.title: Special Cases
specialCases.case1Desc: If you work in Gibraltar but live in Spain, you must declare in both countries. Gibraltar will withhold taxes at source, but you must include this income in your Spanish declaration applying double taxation relief.
specialCases.case2Desc: If you telework part of the time from Spain, taxation can be complex. Consult a tax advisor specializing in these cases.
specialCases.case3Desc: In your first tax year in Gibraltar, you may have to file a proportional return. Make sure to declare your employment start date correctly.

Spain.title: Guide: Tax Return in Spain
Spain.intro: If you work in Gibraltar but live in Spain, or have income in both countries, you must file the IRPF declaration in Spain. This guide explains how to do it correctly applying the double taxation relief.

dates.title: Important Dates (Tax Campaign)
dates.may: May: In-person and phone support begins (exact date varies)
dates.june25: June 25th: If result is to pay with bank direct debit

obliged.title: Are you obliged to declare?
obliged.subtitle: Obliged to declare:
list: Employment income over €22,000/year (one payer)
Over €14,000 with more than one payer (if 2nd exceeds €1,500)
Movable or immovable capital income over €1,600
Capital gains over €1,000
Important: If you work in Gibraltar, you are almost always obliged to declare

dta.title: Double Taxation Agreement Spain-Gibraltar
dta.whatIsDesc: The agreement prevents you from paying taxes twice on the same income. Taxes paid in Gibraltar can be deducted from your Spanish declaration via a tax credit.
steps: Declare all your income in Spain (including Gibraltar)
Calculate Spanish tax on total income
Subtract tax already paid in Gibraltar (tax credit)
Pay the difference (if any) or receive refund
dta.example: Practical Example: If you earn €40,000 in Gibraltar and pay €8,000 taxes there, and Spanish tax on that amount would be €10,000, you would only pay €2,000 extra in Spain.

model100.title: Model 100: Tax Return
model100.intro: Model 100 is the official form for the IRPF declaration. Here we explain the most relevant sections for Gibraltar workers:
model100.sec1Desc: Includes all your labor income, both from Spain and Gibraltar. Use the annual average exchange rate to convert pounds to euros.
model100.sec2Desc: Includes Social Security contributions. If you contribute in Gibraltar, they are also deductible.
model100.sec3Desc: After applying reductions for employment income, deductible expenses, etc.
model100.sec4Desc: Quotas are calculated according to progressive scales of your autonomous community.
model100.sec5Desc: VERY IMPORTANT! Here is where you apply the credit for taxes paid in Gibraltar. You will need a certificate from Gibraltar Income Tax Office regarding payments made there.
model100.sec6Desc: Final result: to pay or to refund. Tax retentions are subtracted.

list: DNI/NIE: Valid Spanish identity document
Spanish Retentions Certificate: If you have income in Spain
Gibraltar Wages Certificate (P60): Issued by your Gibraltar employer
Gibraltar Tax Paid Certificate: From Income Tax Office (essential for double taxation deduction)
Deduction Proofs: Mortgage, donations, pension plans, etc.
Large Family Certificate: If applicable
Bank Details: IBAN for direct debit or refund

steps.title: Steps to File Your Return
steps.s1t: Get your Cl@ve PIN or Digital Certificate
steps.s1d: Required to access Tax Agency website
steps.s3d: AEAT generates an automatic draft, but WILL NOT include your Gibraltar income. You must add it manually.
steps.s4d: In employment income section, add your Gibraltar income converted to euros
steps.s5d: In box 596, enter amount of taxes paid in Gibraltar (with certificate)
steps.s6d: Housing (if applicable), large family, disability, etc.
steps.s7d: Verify all data, save a copy and submit before June 30th

deductions.title: Common Deductions
deductions.housingDesc: Up to 15% of payments (max €9,040/year). Only if purchased before 2013.
deductions.maternityDesc: Up to €1,200/year per child under 3 (working mothers).
deductions.disabilityDesc: Deductions for taxpayer or disabled ascendants/descendants.
deductions.pensionsDesc: Reduce taxable base up to €1,500/year (or €8,500 if >50 years).

specialCases.title: Special Cases
specialCases.geoDesc: If you moved for work, you may be entitled to additional 20% reduction in net income.
specialCases.teleworkDesc: Complex situation. Taxation depends on where work is effectively performed. Consult a specialized tax advisor.
specialCases.residencyDesc: If you changed residence during the year, you may need to file proportional returns or even two returns (Spain and Gibraltar).

regions.title: Differences by Autonomous Community
regions.desc: Each autonomous community has its own IRPF scales and additional deductions:
list: Andalusia: Deductions for birth/adoption, large family, disability
Madrid: Lower scales, deductions for primary residence rent
Catalonia: Deductions for rent, home rehabilitation
Valencia: Deductions for birth, disability, dependents
regions.note: Check specific deductions for your community on your regional tax website.

errors.title: Common Errors to Avoid
errors.e1: Not declaring Gibraltar income: Mandatory. AEAT can detect it and fine you.
errors.e2: Forgetting double taxation deduction: You would be overpaying. Always request certificate in Gibraltar.
errors.e3: Using incorrect exchange rate: Must be official annual average rate (published by Bank of Spain).
errors.e4: Not keeping proofs: Keep all documents at least 4 years in case Tax Agency requires check.
